biography.plain_text: Alfred S.K. Teo is an American manufacturer who founded Sigma Plastics in 1978. He financed its first New Jersey factory by selling his house and borrowing $300,000 through a Small Business Administration loan. The business grew from ten employees into a group producing flexible packaging for industrial, food and retail customers.

confidence.reason: The direct 2010 interview establishes house-sale funding, the SBA amount and initial ten employees. Official company history confirms the founding date and packaging business; the primary securities filing independently establishes United States citizenship.

long_biography.plain_text:
Keeping individual factories independent while sharing central services became a defining feature of Alfred Teo's Sigma Plastics. Local teams specialised in their product markets, with group purchasing, sales and distribution behind them. Shared production capacity and technical resources supported that arrangement. Teo's own responsibilities included ordering machinery and buying raw materials.

The enterprise remained in family ownership as his sons took senior roles: Mark became president and chief executive, and Andrew chief financial officer. All four of his sons have worked in the business. Outside work, Teo has enjoyed tennis, gardening and repairing cars.
